beats.trigger: ## Iterate and Learn
beats.got: nothing new, just a section title.

beats.trigger: to keep iterating as the landscape changes.
beats.got: nothing new.

beats.trigger: Grading its own work is another chance to be helpful: the self-report is the same kind of output as the thing reported on.
beats.got: The AI is too kind when it reviews its own work. That bears on anyone proposing AI to assess performance or hiring.

beats.trigger: Where the account matches what you remember, you have two reads agreeing. Where it doesn't, yours counts.
beats.got: I trust my own judgment over the agent's report when they differ. That is a human-in-the-loop position I can defend to my leadership team.

beats.trigger: Only you could catch a wrong line about you, which is why your own profile is the place to start.
beats.got: The person who knows the subject is the check. So people's expertise still matters, which is the opposite of 'replace headcount'.

beats.trigger: Nobody knows where agents are going, not Anthropic, not your board.
beats.got: Honest, and I respect it. But the line about running the experiment is a bit evangelical, and 'felt experience' is vague.

beats.trigger: The agent updates the file and summarises the changes in chat. Expect the generation rules to change a lot.
beats.got: The agent rereads the rules file against what happened and rewrites it. I'd check every rewrite carefully.

beats.trigger: Repeat on every rules file: do the work → capture → reflect → sharpen.
beats.got: A loop of do, capture, reflect, sharpen. It could become a team habit, like a retrospective.

beats.trigger: Asked the most-uniquely-you line first, the LLM warms into appreciation and goes soft on the generic-line call.
beats.got: Use a second reader without my context, but the explanation of why the order matters lost me. My gut overrides the agent.

beats.got: nothing new.

beats.got: Module 2 wants access to our company systems. I'd have to ask the DPO and works council before connecting anything.

beats.trigger: Karpathy's LLM Wiki post; Lindenberg's memory-architecture piece, optional.
beats.got: Two reading tips, and I don't know either name.

beats.trigger: Arrive with enough real material that the memory starts from your world, not generic output.
beats.got: Prework is a challenge, a source and a plan control, but it never says what 'the memory' is. It does say real material.

beats.trigger: If stuck, scan your next two weeks of calendar; the biggest unresolved item is usually your challenge.
beats.got: Pick one real unresolved problem. Mine would be role design and hiring under the agent shift. Useful, practical advice.

beats.trigger: If a connector needs admin approval, tell the training coordinator and keep going.
beats.got: Connecting the agent to my company's documents means employee data and GDPR. This says only 'ask admin'. I want to ask the DPO first and I'm uneasy that nobody here says so.

beats.trigger: Before it writes anything, ask it for a plan and approve or revise it first.
beats.got: Make the agent show its plan before it touches files. It's a simple control that gives me confidence.

beats.trigger: If a line is blank, name a fallback; do not fill it with a plausible answer.
beats.got: Write three lines and don't invent anything. That ties back to the lesson on plausible filler.

beats.trigger: a useful system is a living pile of text the agent can read, maintain, and improve.
beats.got: A memory is a folder of text the agent reads and updates. Simple enough, but it's more technical than I'd like.

beats.trigger: The output now travels with a file the agent re-reads next time.
beats.got: The rules file carries the lesson from one session to the next. That's the core idea.

take_homes: The AI fills gaps with plausible generic text and also grades its own work too kindly, so I stay the check on anything about people.
Put the lesson in a file the next person's agent reads. That is how a habit can spread from one person to a team.
Show the agent's plan before it writes files, and if I have no real detail to give, say so rather than letting it invent something.

monday.move: Ask my IT lead which agent runtime we already have, and write down my Module 2 challenge: how to handle role design and hiring as agents take on part of the work. I'd use dummy or non-personal data only.
monday.who: Me, then one HR business partner
monday.when: Tuesday, after I've talked to the DPO
monday.stop_condition: Stop if any personal or employee data would go into the tool before the DPO and the works council have agreed.
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and the module doesn't mention either.

misconception.why: I still think agents will change headcount, but the module showed that the agent's output is only as good as the person who knows the subject, so the question may be which tasks change rather than which roles go. I'm not convinced yet.

one_line: Good ideas about checking the AI's work and saving what you learn in a file, but a dozen copies of the same filler paragraph, nothing on what this means for people, and nothing on GDPR or the works council.
